verdict_scope: Source fidelity only: exact current summary compared independently against the complete supplied extracted classic English 1996 rules and matching publisher PDF pages 1–12, including every distinct base Action Card. PASS means no material unsupported rule claim or material omission found within that source; it does not certify a complete procedure for every legal base-game state.
complete_core_explanation: Not a complete-core PASS. Several ordinary base Action Cards still lack definitive mandatory-selection or quantity procedures in reachable states. The summary faithfully discloses these essential source gaps, but disclosure cannot substitute for authoritative missing rulings.

independence.excluded_materials: Questions, answer keys, readers, grades, prior reviews, source-gap register, parent history, expansion pages 13–20, later editions and optional short game were not consulted. No external browsing or reader communication.
independence.method: Read complete summary and complete extracted source; independently used pypdf to extract and read every PDF page 1–12, including embedded card-face text. No rendered-page image inspection was performed.

findings.title: Secret-removal actor participation remains inconsistent
findings.detail: Both removal card faces and headings address fellow players, while their detailed paragraphs require all players to select disks. The summary accurately reports both formulations and does not silently require the selecting player to remove pieces.
findings.gameplay_consequence: The selecting player cannot determine from the supplied source whether they must participate in disk selection, particularly when they have no eligible region. The summary is faithful but does not provide a definitive complete procedure.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an authoritative clarification; do not invent a fallback or treat disclosure as a complete gameplay procedure.

findings.title: Remove-two has no legal-choice procedure in reachable protected-piece states
findings.detail: The detailed rule requires a region with at least two own Caballeros; its singleton fallback is conditioned on at most one in every region. The source also forbids taking from the King's region and Castillo. A player with two in the King's region and singletons elsewhere satisfies neither stated legal procedure. No eligible pieces is also unaddressed.
findings.gameplay_consequence: A base special action may demand a selection that cannot be made under its stated conditions. Summary explicitly discloses this gap.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an authoritative clarification; do not invent a fallback or treat disclosure as a complete gameplay procedure.

findings.title: Remove-all has no legal-choice procedure if all board pieces are protected
findings.detail: The source exempts players with no Caballeros in any region, but otherwise requires selecting a region with at least one while forbidding the King's region. It does not address a player whose only regional pieces are in that protected region.
findings.gameplay_consequence: Affected players can have no legal disk selection without qualifying for the explicit no-regional-pieces exemption.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an authoritative clarification; do not invent a fallback or treat disclosure as a complete gameplay procedure.

findings.title: The King returns lacks a shortfall procedure
findings.detail: The detailed paragraph and embedded card face say each player returns three own pieces from regions and/or court. The bold heading says fellow players, but the summary transparently follows the detail and card face. Neither text specifies what happens with fewer than three eligible pieces; protected pieces cannot be used.
findings.gameplay_consequence: A player may be unable to execute the mandatory quantity. The explicit all-available fallback on the separate Decay of Authority card is not authority to invent the same rule here.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an authoritative clarification; do not invent a fallback or treat disclosure as a complete gameplay procedure.

findings.title: Send-one action lacks an absent-player-piece fallback
findings.detail: The selecting player must return one regional Caballero per player including themselves; the source excludes King's region and Castillo and does not permit court pieces or explain a player with no eligible regional piece.
findings.gameplay_consequence: The action cannot always be executed literally for every player. Summary faithfully identifies the omission.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an authoritative clarification; do not invent a fallback or treat disclosure as a complete gameplay procedure.

findings.title: The Court lacks a province-shortfall procedure
findings.detail: The Court says move two own Caballeros from provinces to court. It gives no explicit instruction for zero or one in provinces. The board-retrieval rule on page 3 belongs to power-card recruitment and is not expressly extended to this action.
findings.gameplay_consequence: A base Action Card has an undefined mandatory quantity when the reserve is insufficient. Summary properly avoids importing recruitment's board retrieval.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an authoritative clarification; do not invent a fallback or treat disclosure as a complete gameplay procedure.

findings.title: Movement disk destinations versus general Castillo permission
findings.detail: The general rule permits any or all moving Caballeros to be put in Castillo. Movement requires affected players to choose another region on disks, which omit Castillo. The source gives no explicit mechanism or exception reconciling those instructions; summary follows the detailed disk procedure and flags the collision.
findings.gameplay_consequence: Whether and how this forced movement can reach Castillo remains unclarified under the supplied source.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an authoritative clarification; do not invent a fallback or treat disclosure as a complete gameplay procedure.

findings.title: All-four scoring with a mobile 4/0/0 at Castillo is not expressly resolved
findings.detail: All-four scoring is based on current first scoreboard value, and mobile scoreboards may be placed at Castillo. Unlike all-five, the all-four paragraph does not expressly discuss Castillo. Summary flags this specific interaction instead of silently declaring inclusion or exclusion.
findings.gameplay_consequence: The source gives no worked case or explicit Castillo statement for this interaction; the audit does not impose a resolution.
findings.recommendation: Obtain an authoritative clarification; do not invent a fallback or treat disclosure as a complete gameplay procedure.

checked_claims.topic: Edition, authors, duration, scope and translation attribution
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: The supplied publisher source names Kramer and Ulrich, 2–5 players, approximately two hours for nine rounds, 1996 copyright and Jay Tummelson translation/editing. Expansion pages and the optional short game were excluded. The omitted sample game sheet/rules booklet are nonessential component-list compression.

King determined by first region card; distinct later cards establish homes; each color has 31 small cubes with ten initially allocated 2 home / 1 score marker / 7 court and 21 provinces. Thirteen power cards and disk excluding Castillo, stacks and mobile scoreboards, marker at 1 and chosen first starter agree.

Five reveals, later round starter is previous last player, clockwise distinct power values, used face-up stacks with only top visible, descending turns, recruitment before card choice, at-most recruitment and insufficient-province board retrieval agree. General taboo and Castillo protection correctly constrain retrieval.

Court deployment and optional special action may be in either order but may not interleave. Number is a maximum, court-to-board destinations are current-King adjacent or Castillo, and selected/unused cards are removed from choices. King returns every round. Castillo quantities announced and removal reserved to general scoring.
No Caballeros, Grande or mobile scoreboard may enter or leave King's region. Scoring is allowed. King movement changes the protected region and current-position adjacency at deployment time.

checked_claims.topic: Stack 1: all own, two extra, and either/or
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: All-own takes all from one eligible origin and expressly permits returning some; two additional own court pieces have unrestricted non-King regional/Castillo destinations; either/or chooses one. Normal one-piece deployment remains distinct.

checked_claims.topic: Stack 1: five, three foreign, any three, two own plus two foreign
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: Single origin and mixed ownership for up-to-five, foreign-only three with multiple eligible origins, any-three ownership and destinations, and separate two-own/two-foreign allowances match. Taboo and Castillo-origin exclusions remain explicit.

checked_claims.topic: Stack 1: four own and any four; destination wording
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: Own-only versus mixed ownership limits and other-regions wording are preserved. The source does not supply a worked multi-origin exchange case; summary avoids inventing an across-all-selected-origins exclusion. All nine distinct intrigue effects are represented, including the effects with duplicate cards.

One incomplete special action, prospective/remainder-only interruption, no undoing completed parts, ordinary deployment immune, announced actions, retained card, same/next round validity and expiry at end of next round match.

Both Decay effects correctly affect fellow players only, with source-stated empty/fewer-than-three handling. King-returns each-player paragraph/card-face attribution, clockwise from left and own-piece choice agree; send-one selector and inclusion of self agree. Secret-removal single-region restrictions and exemptions are recorded without hiding source gaps.
Any region including King's region and Castillo, normal ranks/bonuses, and no Castillo redistribution during a special scoring agree. All eight distinct stack-2 effects are represented.

checked_claims.topic: Stack 3: value categories and mobile scoreboards
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: All printed 4/5/6–7 regional values and names match, including both mobile-board examples and all-five Castillo exclusion. Category and point values follow replacement scoreboard. Special-scoring bonuses apply.

checked_claims.topic: Stack 3: Castillo, first-only, most, least and any region
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: Castillo is re-covered over same pieces, first-place ties score zero, first-only excludes Castillo, most includes all tied regions, least excludes empty regions and Castillo, and any-region includes King/Castillo. All eight distinct stack-3 effects are represented.
Scoreboard may be introduced or relocated including Castillo, cannot cross King-region boundary, cannot stack, and must show 8/4/0 or 4/0/0 upright. Adviser has neighboring-region range.

Fellow players move all own pieces from selected eligible region, secret simultaneous disk choices, King/origin choices route to court, and protected origin exclusions match. The broad Castillo interaction is explicitly disclosed separately.

Grande cannot enter or leave King's region, cannot enter Castillo, may join other Grandes and establishes a new home. Recovery is one any played power card including current card, without mandatory disclosure.

checked_claims.topic: Stack 4: The Court and unique scoring
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: The Court origin/destination and two-own quantity match with shortfall unspecified. Every player chooses a disk region simultaneously for scoring, King's region allowed, Castillo omitted by disk, duplicate choices not scored. All seven distinct stack-4 effects are represented.
Single card has five normal deployments plus optional King placement in any region except Castillo; adjacency depends on order/current position.

checked_claims.topic: General scoring order and complete emptying
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: Secret destination before uncovering; score Castillo; reveal/move all of each color to one region; return illegal King choices to court; replace Castillo empty; then score nine regions in track order. Illegal-choice consequence does not legalize prohibited selection.

checked_claims.topic: Region ranks, player counts and classic tie examples
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: Grande contributes zero; 2-player first-only, 3-player first-two, other counts first-three; tied ranks shift down one. Both numerical examples exactly match this edition, including compressed ranks in its three-way first tie. Two-player tied first gets no payable rank.
Both +2 require sole regional majority, home bonus requires majority holder's own Grande, both may apply in special scorings, and neither is paid on first tie. Grande can change home via its action.

checked_claims.topic: End condition and additional tie rule
checked_claims.evidence_and_assessment: All third-general-scoring stages complete before game ends; furthest success marker wins; no extra endgame tiebreaker is supplied in the source.

The summary labels open procedures, distinguishes the inconsistent headings/card text where relevant, and does not authorize protected-piece removal or import later-edition rulings. These disclosures preserve fidelity but do not close the gameplay gaps.

source_limitations.qualification: These are source limitations, not findings that the summary invented these rules. Some have plausible natural readings, but no complete-core certification should silently adopt a missing fallback. Printed board adjacency, scoring-track order and regional scoreboards remain physical game references; the summary need not reproduce the whole board.
